Two ways to work with Lumen. Index makes a conversation readable and inspectable. Studio gives sustained drafting its own working space beside the response. Both use the same three-layer composer, actual model picker, tools, drafts and routing owners.

Actual local application screenshots · clearly synthetic account and conversation · 20 October 2026 · no live inference, physical-iPhone claim, production visual integration or deployment. All 26 curated images are embedded in this file.

Index · Workspace & composer

Substantive changes

Index: a working-document heading, quieter brief and structured response replace the bubble hierarchy. The intelligence margin contains a navigable answer outline, current route evidence and a compact context estimate. Phones keep reading central and expose intelligence contextually.

Studio: a persistent writing station and independently scrolling response share the desktop. Expansion reallocates space to writing. On phones, writing mode takes the available viewport, keeps its actions visible and returns to the conversation.

Shared composer: context and truthful tool states above writing; real Auto/manual/Layout selection, a labelled estimate and Send/Stop below. Expansion keeps the same textarea, draft, caret and selection. Wordmark-first treatments remain proposals; no symbol is presented as approved.

Try these interactions

  1. Enter a multiline draft and select a phrase. Expand and collapse: preserve the exact draft and selection. Escape in the editor returns to reading.
  2. Switch Auto → a manual model → Launch writing. Open usage and Routing Center, then return: the draft and selected route remain.
  3. Toggle Search and Research; attach and remove a text file. Unsupported Research is disabled when no Gemini model is enabled. Nothing sends until Send.
  4. In Index, use the answer outline with keyboard Enter. In Studio, scroll a long draft and the response independently.

Screenshots are offline evidence, not interactive product replicas. Reproduce actual controls with the guarded local fixture described in README.md. Manual preview denies external inference; automated tests alone intercept a synthetic Send/Stop request.

Evidence and open weaknesses

Chromium and Linux WebKit workflows cover 1440×960 and390×844, plus narrow320px and reduced-height writing. Checks cover selection/focus, keyboard activation, tools, attachments, real model and Layout switching, known/unknown allowance provenance, masked settings, policy persistence and one explicit synthetic Send/Stop per case. Each captured state receives an automated accessibility scan.

Reduced viewport resizing simulates keyboard space. It does not verify a physical iPhone, keyboard animation, safe-area/browser chrome behavior or native touch feel. No live-provider, billing or authentication conclusions are drawn.

Proof-only portals and CSS are exploration scaffolding. A production version needs approved shared components/tokens, a complete complex-state/theme/zoom/device matrix and further brand/motion refinement. The answer outline currently targets rendered Markdown headings; very long virtualized history requires a canonical navigation integration.

Gate 1 remains unapproved. These are reviewable workspace directions, not a final brand, approved design system or completed Blackout rollout. Existing strict-audit production findings remain documented. No main merge or deployment was attempted.

Routing Center screenshots retain the verified provider browser. The separate provider-review.html preserves its detailed ordinary and keyboard-focus evidence. Original-app comparisons use the identical conversation, short draft and viewport without experimental CSS.
